q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance (Revenue)

**(a) Time left until resolution:**
The earnings release is scheduled for August 26, 2026. Today is August 21, 2026. **5 days remain** until the announcement.

**(b) Most likely outcome and why:**

This is an exceptionally narrow forecasting window. NVIDIA will provide forward guidance during its Q2 FY2027 earnings call on August 26, 2026. The research provides clear, recent guidance data:

- **NVIDIA's official Q2 FY2027 guidance (issued May 20, 2026):** $91.0 billion ± 2%, yielding a range of $89.2B to $92.8B
- **Analyst consensus:** Around $91.9 billion (roughly 1% above midpoint), with some aggregators suggesting $93.5 billion
- **Q1 FY2027 actual result:** $81.6 billion, beating guidance by ~$2 billion

The question asks for "forward guidance" in the Q2 FY2027 *earnings release*, which means guidance for the *subsequent quarter* (Q3 FY2027), not Q2 itself. This is standard practice—companies provide both actual results for the period just completed and forward guidance for the next quarter.

However, given the uncertainty around what "forward guidance" refers to specifically, I interpret this most naturally as asking: what will NVIDIA guide for Q3 FY2027 revenue when it reports Q2 FY2027 results on August 26?

Given:
- Strong sequential growth momentum ($81.6B in Q1 → $91.0B guidance for Q2 represents ~11.5% QoQ growth)
- Demand for AI chips remains robust
- The company beat Q1 guidance by ~$2B, suggesting conservative guidance patterns
- Analyst consensus places Q2 FY2027 near the upper end of guidance ($91.9B–$93.5B)

If Q2 actual results align with or exceed the $89.2B–$92.8B range, NVIDIA's Q3 FY2027 forward guidance would likely show continued sequential growth. Historical patterns suggest Q3 guidance could be in the range of **$99B–$105B** based on typical growth trajectories, though this remains speculative without actual Q2 results.

The given range for this question (99.5B to 115.5B) encompasses plausible guidance scenarios for the next quarter.

**(c) What would push the value lower?**

- Stronger-than-expected competitive pressures from AMD, Intel, or other chipmakers
- Macro headwinds or a slowdown in AI capex spending by hyperscalers
- Geopolitical restrictions further limiting China revenue (already excluded from current guidance)
- Supply chain disruptions affecting H100/H200 production
- A miss on Q2 FY2027 actual results, causing management to reduce Q3 guidance

**(d) What would push the value higher?**

- Q2 FY2027 actual results significantly exceed the upper end of guidance (continuing the ~$2B beat pattern from Q1)
- Accelerating AI adoption and data center expansion driving higher capex forecasts
- Better-than-expected product mix or ASP (average selling price) dynamics
- Geopolitical developments allowing incremental China revenue
- Stronger-than-expected forward orders and bookings for Q3 and beyond

**(e) Base rate or historical reference values:**

The research provides NVIDIA's recent guidance trajectory:
- **Q1 FY2027 guidance:** Not explicitly stated, but actual was $81.6B (beat by ~$2B)
- **Q2 FY2027 guidance:** $91.0B ± 2% ($89.2B–$92.8B)

This represents sequential growth. Typical enterprise datacenter chip suppliers grow 10–15% QoQ during strong demand periods. Applied to a $91B+ Q2, Q3 FY2027 guidance would logically fall in the **$100B–$105B range** as a baseline extrapolation, assuming continued momentum.

---

## Probability Distribution Estimate

Given only 5 days until announcement and that forward guidance is typically directional and conservative relative to actual results:

- **Central estimate:** ~$102 billion (representing ~12% QoQ growth from $91B midpoint, consistent with recent trajectory)
- **Lower bound risk:** Could dip to $99–$100B if Q2 results disappoint or macro concerns emerge
- **Upper bound risk:** Could reach $108–$112B if Q2 beats significantly and demand signals remain robust

The range 99.5B to 115.5B brackets reasonable outcomes. My 10th, 50th, and 90th percentiles:

Low (10th percentile): 99500000000
Median (50th percentile): 103000000000
High (90th percentile): 110000000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is scheduled to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26, 2026. For Q2 FY2027, NVIDIA's own guidance, issued on May 20, 2026, projects revenue of $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This implies a range with a ceiling near $92.8 billion and a floor near $89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

This guidance explicitly excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Analysts' average estimates for Q2 FY2027 revenue are around $91.9 billion, placing it within NVIDIA's guidance range, about 1% above the midpoint [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), [ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026). Some aggregators, however, peg revenue nearer $93.5 billion [ifyouspent.com](https://news.ifyouspent.com/en/news/nvidia-earnings-what-to-watch-august-2026/). For Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported $81.6 billion, exceeding its own guidance by approximately $2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
